newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Eight Israeli troops wounded in south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Eight Israeli troops wounded in south Lebanon.

text.p: Eight Israeli soldiers were wounded on Wednesday in two separate incidents in the south Lebanon border zone occupied by the Jewish state, Israeli security sources said.
Five soldiers were wounded in a late-afternoon clash with guerrillas in the central sector of zone. No other details were immediately available. The army said it was checking the report.

Earlier on Wednesday, a mine exploded in the buffer strip's eastern sector, wounding three Israeli soldiers. Security sources said one soldier was in fair condition and the other two were lightly wounded.
On Tuesday, Moslem guerrillas attacked Israeli and allied militia posts and some shells slammed into two villages in the zone, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
The Iranian-backed Hizbollah -- Party of God -- claimed responsibility for Tuesday's attacks. It said its gunners targetted two military barracks in Aishiyeh and Rihane villages.

Hizbollah is leading a guerrilla war against Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong South Lebanon Army militia holding the 15-km (nine-miles) south Lebanon zone set up in 1985 to protect northern Israel from cross-frontier raids.
The violence coincided with the conclusion of a three-day meeting of a five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in the area.
The monitoring group comprising the United States, France, Lebanon, Syria and Israel urged Israeli forces and Hizbollah guerrillas to stay clear of civilian areas in their tit-for-tat war.
The group discussed three complaints each by Lebanon and Israel over recent alleged breaches of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in April.
Both sides accused the other of shelling civilian villages inside or outside Israel's occupation zone.
